questions.stem: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay that begins with the sentence " As requirements for job applications are getting increasingly higher, college students ought to be better prepared for their future career. " You can make comments, cite examples or use your personal experiences to develop your essay. You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words. You should copy the sentence given in quotes at the beginning of your essay.
questions.analysis:
【参考范文】
As requirements for job applications are getting increasingly higher, college students ought to be better prepared for their future career. In an era when employers demand not only a diploma but also practical competence, waiting until graduation to think about work is simply too late.

There are concrete steps every student can take. To begin with, obtaining relevant certificates and mastering professional skills builds a solid foundation. Last summer, for instance, I taught myself data analysis and earned a certificate, which later helped me stand out in an internship interview. What is more, internships offer irreplaceable experience: by working in a real company, students learn how a workplace actually operates and discover which career truly suits them. Such preparation turns abstract knowledge into employable ability.

In conclusion, the fiercer competition becomes, the more valuable early preparation is. Therefore, college students should seize every chance to enrich their skills and experience, so that when opportunity knocks, they are ready to open the door.

transcript.text: M: Good morning. My name is Bob Fetterman. I'm the computer technician.
transcript.zh: M：早上好。我叫鲍勃·费特曼，是电脑技术员。

transcript.text: W: Didn't I call for you last week?
transcript.zh: W：上周不是我打电话叫你来的吗？

transcript.text: M: Maybe? I work for Alpha Maintenance. I imagine someone from your office called our central office and I'm the engineer designated to your case.
transcript.zh: M：可能吧？我为 Alpha Maintenance 工作。我想应该是你们办公室有人打电话给了我们的总部，而我是负责处理你们这个问题的工程师。

transcript.text: W: Yeah, I spoke to a lady there last Tuesday, which is now 10 days ago. I made it clear it was an urgent matter and please send someone as soon as possible. Couldn't you or someone else have come sooner?
transcript.zh: W：是的，我上周二，也就是十天前，跟那边的一位女士谈过。我明确说过这是件急事，请尽快派人过来。你或者其他人就不能早点来吗？

transcript.text: M: I'm sorry, but I'm not in charge of scheduling all logistics. I simply do not know. All I can tell you is I got the call this week and came as soon as I could.
transcript.zh: M：很抱歉，但我不负责安排所有的后勤事宜。我确实不知道。我只能告诉你，我是这周接到电话的，并且已经尽可能快地赶来了。

transcript.text: W: I see. Well, I'll have you know, my manager is rather indignant that it's taken you this long to come. I understand it might not be your fault, but nevertheless, you should know what the feeling is around here.
transcript.zh: W：我明白了。不过我要告诉你，我的经理对你们花了这么长时间才过来相当不满。我知道这可能不是你的错，但不管怎样，你应该知道这里对此事的看法。

transcript.text: M: I understand, and I'm sorry for any inconvenience. I will try to resolve your computer problem as swiftly and optimally as I can. What and where is the issue?
transcript.zh: M：我明白，也很抱歉给你带来不便。我会尽我所能，尽快、妥善地解决你们的电脑问题。问题是什么，在哪里？

transcript.text: W: It's this machine right here. It was running slow for a while, I guess, and gradually got worse and worse. Last Tuesday, it just stopped working altogether. If you switch it on, you will see what I mean.
transcript.zh: W：就是这台机器。它运行缓慢有一阵子了，我想，然后逐渐变得越来越糟。上周二，它彻底停止工作了。你把它打开就知道我说的是什么意思了。

transcript.text: M: Okay. Do you know if it's backed up?
transcript.zh: M：好的。你知道它有没有备份吗？

transcript.text: W: Backed up?
transcript.zh: W：备份？

transcript.text: M: I mean, do you know if its contents have been copied and saved somewhere else?
transcript.zh: M：我的意思是，你知道里面的内容有没有被复制并保存到其他地方吗？

transcript.text: W: I don't know.
transcript.zh: W：我不知道。

transcript.text: M: Well, depending on the ensuing operative scenario, if I need to wipe the system directories clean in order to reconfigure default protocols, then my first intervention should be to intricately retrieve all inventories that I can. Otherwise, all data that was stored on its hard drive will be forever lost.
transcript.zh: M：这个嘛，具体要看接下来采取什么操作。如果我需要清空系统目录，以便重新配置默认协议，那么我的第一步应该是尽可能仔细地找回所有资料。否则，存储在硬盘上的所有数据都会永久丢失。

transcript.text: W: My manager would know. Let me go get him.
transcript.zh: W：我的经理应该知道。我去把他叫来。

transcript.text: M: Have you given more thought to studying law?
transcript.zh: M: 你有没有进一步考虑过学法律？

transcript.text: W: I've been thinking about it a lot, yes. In fact, this is why I wished to speak to you. I wanted to hear more about what it's like.
transcript.zh: W: 我确实认真考虑过很多次。事实上，这就是我想和你谈谈的原因。我想多了解一下这个职业到底是什么样的。

transcript.text: M: A career in law is a beautiful thing in my opinion. Many people will say it's a boring field, but I disagree. The thing is there are many different branches of law and many different jobs.
transcript.zh: M: 在我看来，从事法律工作是一件很美好的事。很多人会说这是个无聊的领域，但我不这么认为。问题在于，法律有许多不同的分支，也有许多不同的工作。

transcript.text: W: You are involved with buildings and construction, right?
transcript.zh: W: 你是从事建筑和施工方面工作的，对吧？

transcript.text: M: Correct. I'm a solicitor, specializing in real estate. Most of my work involves mediating land disputes.
transcript.zh: M: 没错。我是一名事务律师，专门从事房地产法律事务。我的大部分工作都涉及调解土地纠纷。

transcript.text: W: Do you mind giving me an example?
transcript.zh: W: 你介意举个例子吗？

transcript.text: M: Sure. So in many cases I am employed to arbitrate between two clashing parties. Let's say for example, there are two landowners who are in a thorny disagreement about something like the borders of their adjacent plots. Someone may employ me to break the deadlock and resolve the dispute. Often my work involves negotiating agreements, plain and simple.
transcript.zh: M: 当然可以。很多时候，我会受雇在两个发生冲突的当事人之间进行仲裁。比如说，有两位土地所有者，因为相邻地块的边界之类的问题而陷入棘手的争执。有人可能会聘请我来打破僵局，解决这场纠纷。很多时候，我的工作就是协商达成协议，仅此而已。

transcript.text: W: So you are saying that a lot of what you do is fix people's legal issues, like you try to find a solution that benefits everyone and that prevents a problem from escalating.
transcript.zh: W: 所以你的意思是，你所做的很多事情都是在解决人们的法律问题，比如努力找到一个对大家都有利的解决方案，防止问题进一步恶化。

transcript.text: M: Exactly, well put. You need to remember that courts, like all bureaucracies really, can be very messy, frustrating, and expensive. For this reason, it's usually better to resolve problems outside of court whenever possible.
transcript.zh: M: 没错，你说得很准确。你要记住，法院和所有官僚机构一样，往往会非常混乱、令人沮丧，而且费用高昂。因此，只要有可能，通常最好在法院之外解决问题。

transcript.text: W: I see. So besides knowing the law inside out, you need good people skills, right?
transcript.zh: W: 我明白了。所以除了要对法律了如指掌之外，还需要有很好的人际交往能力，对吧？

transcript.text: M: Of course. Any job that involves people requires good interpersonal skills, and any law professional needs to be very eloquent at articulating that argument.
transcript.zh: M: 当然。任何涉及与人打交道的工作都需要良好的人际交往能力，而任何法律从业者都需要非常善于清晰、有说服力地表达自己的观点。

transcript.text: W: Right. So I've been thinking about studying criminal law. I think it sounds very interesting.
transcript.zh: W: 对。所以我一直在考虑学习刑法。我觉得这听起来很有意思。

transcript.text: M: Mm-hmm, yes. I'd say there's more money in property law, but the stakes are higher in criminal law. I can see how you would find it more interesting.
transcript.zh: M: 嗯，是的。我想房地产法能赚更多钱，但刑法涉及的利害关系更大。我能理解你为什么会觉得它更有趣。

optionAnalysis.C: 张冠李戴：It's a beautiful thing. 盗用了录音原话 a beautiful thing in my opinion，但那是男士『我个人』的看法，题干问的是 many people 怎么说——把说话人的观点安到『许多人』头上，归属错位。

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P11）：Any job that involves people requires good interpersonal skills, and any law professional needs to be very eloquent at articulating that argument.信号：要求信号 needs to be 。题干问 required of any law professional，录音 any law professional needs to be very eloquent at …

transcript.text: When a person tries to access a memory, their brains quickly examine everything stored in it to find the relevant information. But as we age, many of us have difficulty retrieving memories.
transcript.zh: 当一个人试图提取一段记忆时，其大脑会迅速检查其中储存的所有内容，以找出相关信息。但随着年龄增长，我们中的许多人会难以回忆起记忆。

transcript.text: In a review published in the journal *Trends in Cognitive Sciences* on February 11th, researchers propose an explanation for why this might be happening: the brains of older adults allocate more space to accumulated knowledge and have more material to navigate when attempting to access memories. While this wealth of prior knowledge can make memory retrieval challenging, the researchers say it has its upsides—this life experience can aid with creativity and decision-making.
transcript.zh: 研究人员在2月11日发表于《认知科学趋势》杂志的一篇综述中提出了这一现象可能发生的原因：老年人的大脑会为积累的知识分配更多空间，因此在尝试提取记忆时需要在更多内容中进行搜索。研究人员表示，尽管这些丰富的既有知识会使记忆提取变得更具挑战性，但它也有积极的一面——这些人生经历能够帮助人们进行创造和决策。

transcript.text: Researchers Tarek Amer, Jordana Wynn and Lynn Hasher looked at several behavioral and brain imaging studies, which show that older adults have difficulty suppressing information that is no longer relevant and that when searching for a specific memory, they often retrieve other, irrelevant memories along with it. The studies also showed that when given a cognitive task, older adults rely more heavily on previous knowledge than younger adults do.
transcript.zh: 研究人员塔雷克·阿梅尔、乔丹娜·温和林恩·哈舍尔考察了多项行为研究和脑成像研究。这些研究显示，老年人难以抑制已经不再相关的信息；在寻找某一特定记忆时，他们常常会连同其他无关记忆一起提取出来。研究还显示，在面对认知任务时，老年人比年轻人更加依赖既有知识。

transcript.text: While the researchers focus primarily on the difficulties that these disorderly, crowded memories may pose, they also highlight a few situations in which these same memory patterns may be useful. "Evidence suggests that older adults show preserved, and at times enhanced, creativity as a function of enriched memories," the researchers write. They further hypothesize that older adults may be well served by their prior knowledge when it comes to decision-making, where they can pull on their accumulated wisdom.
transcript.zh: 尽管研究人员主要关注这些杂乱、拥挤的记忆可能造成的困难，但他们也指出了几种相同记忆模式可能发挥作用的情形。研究人员写道：“证据表明，老年人的创造力得益于记忆内容的丰富，不仅得以保持，有时还会有所增强。”他们进一步推测，在进行决策时，老年人可能会受益于自己的既有知识，因为他们能够运用积累的智慧。

questions.stem: What did the researchers do in their review in the journal Trends in Cognitive Sciences?

options.text: They looked into the relationship between one's prior knowledge and creativity.
They offered novel ways to help older adults to keep their memories from aging.
They proposed an explanation for old people's difficulty in retrieving memories.
They advanced a new model concerning human information storage and retrieval.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P2）：researchers propose an explanation for why this might be happening: the brains of older adults allocate more space to accumulated knowledge and have more material to navigate when attempting to access memories.信号：研究行为动词 propose 。定位信号是描述研究者行为的那个动词 propose an explanation for why this might be happening——题干问 do（做了什么），原文里紧跟…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：A 项 looked into the relationship between one's prior knowledge and creativity 盗用了原文确实出现过的 prior knowledge 与 creativity（见第四段 enhanced, creativity），但那是后文讲记忆模式的好处时顺带提到的，研究综述本身做的核心动作是 propose an explanation，不是去研究知识与创造力的关系，属听到原词就想选的陷阱。 借用原文：propose an explanation for why this might be happening
optionAnalysis.B: 未提及：B 项 offered novel ways to help older adults to keep their memories from aging 借用了 older adults、memories 等话题词，但原文从头到尾只是提出解释、分析现象，没有任何研究者提供新方法去防止记忆衰老的内容，属未提及。
optionAnalysis.D: 偷换概念：D 项 advanced a new model concerning human information storage and retrieval 用 retrieval 这个原文反复出现的词制造熟悉感，但原文研究者做的是 propose an explanation（提出一个解释），不是 advance a new model（提出一个新模型）；一个解释和一个新模型不是同一层级的成果，属偷换概念。
optionAnalysis.C: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（propose an explanation for why this might be happening ↔ proposed an explanation 近乎同词的动作）

transcript.text: There are at least four major problems with work in America today.
transcript.zh: 如今，美国的工作至少存在四个主要问题。

transcript.text: First, work can be alienating. Workers are often not in control of how they work, when they work, what is done with the goods and services they produce, and what is done with the profits made from their work.
transcript.zh: 首先，工作可能导致异化。劳动者往往无法掌控自己的工作方式、工作时间、对其生产的商品和服务的处置方式，以及对其劳动所创造利润的处置方式。

transcript.text: Second, workers are not paid the full value of their labor. Real wages have not kept pace with productivity, driving economic inequality and a decline in labor's share of income.
transcript.zh: 其次，劳动者没有获得其劳动的全部价值。实际工资未能与生产率同步增长，导致经济不平等加剧，并使劳动收入在总收入中的占比下降。

transcript.text: Third, people are time poor. In the U.S., full time employees work an average of 8.72 hours per day despite productivity increases. Long working hours contribute to the feeling of "time poverty", which has an adverse effect on psychological well-being.
transcript.zh: 第三，人们缺乏时间。尽管生产率有所提高，美国的全职雇员每天平均工作8.72小时。长时间工作加剧了“时间贫困”感，并对心理健康产生不利影响。

transcript.text: Fourth, automation puts jobs and wages at risk. Technological innovation could in theory liberate people from the 40-hour work week. But unless changes are made to the structure of work, automation will simply exert downward pressure on wages and further diminish work opportunities.
transcript.zh: 第四，自动化使工作岗位和工资面临风险。从理论上说，技术创新可以使人们摆脱每周40小时的工作制。但是，除非对工作结构进行改变，否则自动化只会给工资施加下行压力，并进一步减少工作机会。

transcript.text: So, what can be done to alleviate these problems? There are competing visions of the best way to arrive at a solution. One vision is what's known as the "post-work" position. The post-work theorists believe that work should not hold a central position in our lives or take up so much of our time. They assert that although doing some work might be necessary, meaning, purpose and social value reside in the communities and relationships built and sustained outside of the workplace. Thus, life should be seen as an end in itself.
transcript.zh: 那么，可以采取什么措施来缓解这些问题呢？对于如何实现解决方案，人们存在相互竞争的构想。其中一种构想被称为“后工作”立场。后工作理论家认为，工作不应在我们的生活中占据核心地位，也不应占用我们如此多的时间。他们主张，尽管从事一定的工作可能是必要的，但意义、目标和社会价值存在于工作场所以外建立并维系的社区和关系之中。因此，生活本身应被视为目的。

transcript.text: Recent studies show that self-control and persistence increase academic outcomes, independence of IQ. Even our personal beliefs about efforts can affect academic outcomes. Children who think effort leads to achievement outperform those who believe ability is a fixed trait. Given the link between persistence and academic success, decisions about efforts are particularly important in childhood.
transcript.zh: 近期研究表明，自我控制和坚持不懈能够提升学业表现，而这一作用独立于智商。甚至我们对努力的个人看法也会影响学业表现。认为努力能够带来成就的儿童，比那些认为能力是一种固定特质的儿童表现更好。鉴于坚持不懈与学业成功之间的联系，童年时期对是否付出努力的判断尤为重要。

transcript.text: Yet, relatively little research has explored how young children learn what's worth the effort. We all know that infants are keen observers of the social world, but they're not just idly watching; they are tiny learning machines. They can generalize such abstract concepts as causal relationships and social roles from just a few examples. Even a 15-month-old infant can outperform a high level computer in such tasks. Could infants also make broad generalizable inferences from a few examples when it comes to effort? If so, then maybe persistence isn't simply a character trait. Maybe it's flexible and adaptable based on social context.
transcript.zh: 然而，相对而言，很少有研究探讨幼儿是如何学会判断什么值得付出努力的。我们都知道，婴儿善于观察社会世界，但他们并非只是无所事事地观看；他们是微型的学习机器。他们仅凭几个例子，就能概括出因果关系和社会角色等抽象概念。即使是15个月大的婴儿，在这类任务中的表现也可能超过高水平的计算机。当涉及努力时，婴儿是否也能根据少数几个例子作出广泛且可推广的推断？如果可以，那么坚持不懈也许并不只是某种性格特征，而是会根据社会情境灵活调整、适应变化的能力。

transcript.text: To explore this question, we showed 15-month-old babies one of two things—an experimenter working hard to achieve two different goals, or an experimenter who effortlessly reached each goal. Then we introduced the baby to a novel music toy that seemed as if it could be activated by pushing a big button on top. The button could be pressed down, but didn't actually activate anything. Out of sight of the babies, we turned on the music toy with a hidden button so that they heard the toy making music. We gave the babies the music toy and left the room. Then analysts who didn't know which condition each baby was in, watched video tapes of the experiment and counted how many times babies tried to activate the toy by pressing the button.
transcript.zh: 为了探究这一问题，我们向15个月大的婴儿展示两种情形中的一种：一名实验者努力工作以实现两个不同的目标，或者一名毫不费力地实现每个目标的实验者。随后，我们向婴儿介绍一个新颖的音乐玩具，看起来似乎可以通过按下顶部的大按钮来启动。这个按钮可以被按下，但实际上并不会启动任何功能。在婴儿看不见的地方，我们用一个隐藏按钮打开了音乐玩具，让他们听到玩具发出音乐。我们把音乐玩具交给婴儿，然后离开房间。之后，不知道每个婴儿属于哪种实验条件的分析人员观看了实验录像，并统计婴儿试图通过按下按钮启动玩具的次数。

transcript.text: Across one study and a pre-registered duplication, babies who had seen an adult persist and succeed push the button about twice as many times as those who saw an adult effortlessly succeed. In other words, babies learned that effort was valuable after watching just two examples of an adult working hard and succeeding. Part of what's exciting about this finding is that the babies didn't just imitate the adult's actions. Instead, they generalized the value of effort to a novel task. The experimenter never demonstrated pushing a button or trying to make music. Instead, the babies learned from different examples of effortful actions that the new toy probably also required persistence.
transcript.zh: 在一项研究及其预注册重复实验中，看过成年人坚持不懈并取得成功的婴儿，按下按钮的次数约为看过成年人毫不费力地取得成功的婴儿的两倍。换言之，婴儿仅仅观察成年人努力工作并取得成功的两个例子后，就学会了努力是有价值的。这一发现令人兴奋的部分原因在于，婴儿并不只是模仿成年人的动作。相反，他们把努力的价值推广到了一个全新的任务中。实验者从未示范按按钮或尝试让玩具播放音乐。相反，婴儿从不同的努力行为示例中学到，这个新玩具可能也需要坚持不懈。

transcript.text: Sometimes Bostonians seem like they're just too busy to be polite. Why is their city like that? Former U.S. representative Chester Atkins says it's because the Puritan founding fathers were themselves impatient and bad-tempered, and had little time for courtesy. That culture has carried down to the present day, he believes. Boston College professor Thomas O'Connor thinks a contributing factor is Boston's history as a city where each new group of immigrants was treated with suspicion and exclusion. That's given Boston a sense of clannishness and reserve, he thinks. The idea of a stranger greeting another stranger is simply not part of the local culture, he says. People will begin a conversation with someone they know, but not with a stranger. Ralph Whitehead, a professor of journalism at the University of Massachusetts at Amherst, thinks it's because Boston's upper class used manners to make class distinctions. By being snobbish about manners, Proper Bostonians made other people scornful of courtesy, he says.

paragraphs.text:
In her second year, Charlene Duong learned of the use of poisonous, synthetic pesticides on her college campus. Shocked but not surprised, she knew she had to do something. Along with a couple of classmates, Charlene did a quick web search and discovered a small but growing movement led by the organization, Herbicide-Free Campus (HFC), to rid college campuses of artificial herbicides(灭草剂). They were 26______ .

Like many, Charlene experiences climate anxiety—a 27______ fear of a climate catastrophe—and was, at the time, looking for an 28______ . When she discovered the HFC movement, she said she felt she "had found a specific area to focus on that still fit into the larger picture of fighting for a healthier, safer, cleaner 29______ for all."

Toxic herbicide use in university land care is not unique. Most institutions of higher education rely on synthetic pesticides and fertilizers to achieve 30______ goals. Having a "beautiful" campus means green and perfectly maintained lawns along with flower beds and paved sidewalks. But these 31______ managed campuses can come at a cost: increased cancer risk, 32______ waterways, poisoned wildlife and lifeless soil.

Pesticide use on college campuses also contributes to our global climate crisis. The use of chemicals to get rid of insects or unwanted plant life can increase indirect 33______ as they can include petroleum-based ingredients. Pesticide use also decreases the life in soil, 34______ the ability of soils to absorb carbon or retain water and thus reducing campuses' ability to recover quickly from climate-related extreme weather events like droughts and floods.

Instead of using toxic chemicals, students working with HFC help out with 35______ the campus grounds.

"This work reminds me to be in the present moment as I play my role in reducing herbicide use and keeping my campus safe and healthy," says Charlene.

questions.stem: Choose the word for blank 26.
questions.analysis:
【答案】J（官方答案）
应填 J) intrigued
【原文】上文 discovered a small but growing movement 表明她们发现了一个新兴运动；They were __(26)__ 紧承其后，自然描述她们对这场运动**产生浓厚兴趣**的状态。be intrigued 是描述人被某事吸引的经典搭配。
A) aesthetic '她们是美学的'语义不通：aesthetic 修饰物的审美属性，不用于描述人的情绪反应，'They were aesthetic'语义荒谬。
C) contaminated '她们被污染了'语义不合：contaminated 修饰水/土等物质或抽象意义的'被污染的（思想）'，描述这群积极投身环保的学生，方向完全相反。
K) juvenile 幼稚的与积极行动矛盾：juvenile 含贬义，会把这群有担当的大学生贬为'幼稚'，与全段她们果决行动的基调冲突。

questions.stem: Choose the word for blank 27.
questions.analysis:
【答案】B（官方答案）
应填 B) chronic
【原文】破折号后是对 climate anxiety 的同位解释。气候焦虑本质上是一种**长期、持续**的恐惧，chronic fear（慢性恐惧）是心理学常用搭配，正好刻画这种持续不消退的状态，与 'climate anxiety' 的本义对应。
A) aesthetic 审美的不能修饰 fear：aesthetic 指审美/美学的，与恐惧情绪无逻辑关系，搭配不成立。
C) contaminated 被污染的不修饰情绪：contaminated 用于水、土壤等被污染的物质，不能修饰 fear 这种抽象情绪。
J) intrigued 感兴趣的修饰人不修饰 fear：intrigued 表'被深深吸引的'，主语通常是人，且与恐惧情绪在情感色彩上相反。
K) juvenile 幼稚的与气候焦虑色彩冲突：juvenile 表'少年的/幼稚的'，带贬义，会把气候焦虑矮化为'孩子气的恐惧'，与下文积极行动的语调相悖。

questions.stem: Choose the word for blank 28.
questions.analysis:
【答案】L（官方答案）
应填 L) outlet
【原文】上文 Charlene experiences climate anxiety—a __(27)__ fear of a climate catastrophe 说她有气候焦虑，下文 she felt she "had found a specific area to focus on" 表明她找到了可投入精力的具体领域——这正是焦虑情绪的**释放出口**（outlet）。look for an outlet 是描述情绪宣泄的固定搭配。
I) infringement 侵权不是被'寻找'的对象：look for an infringement（寻找一项侵权行为）在语义上荒谬，且与 climate anxiety 的语境完全脱节。
N) vibrations 辅音开头不能跟 an：vibrations 以辅音 /v/ 开头，先被 an 拒之门外；且词义与气候焦虑无关。

questions.stem: Choose the word for blank 29.
questions.analysis:
【答案】F（官方答案）
应填 F) environment
【原文】healthier、safer、cleaner 是描述**生存环境**的高频搭配三件套，a healthier, safer, cleaner __(29)__ for all 整句承接上文 fighting for，正是为所有人争取一个更健康、安全、洁净的**环境**，与全文反对除草剂、保护校园生态的主旨完全吻合。
E) emissions 排放物不能被'更健康'修饰：emissions 指废气排放物，搭配 healthier/safer/cleaner 在语义上矛盾——人们要的是减少排放，而不是'更健康的排放'。
I) infringement 侵权与三形容词南辕北辙：infringement 指对权利的侵犯，是负面行为，无法用 healthier/safer/cleaner 来修饰，且与本文话题无关。
L) outlet 释放渠道与'更健康'不搭：outlet 指情绪/精力的发泄出口，是个体层面的概念，不能用 healthier/safer/cleaner for all 这种宏观三连修饰。
N) vibrations 振动与文章话题无关：vibrations 指物理振动，与气候、校园生态无关，纯粹凑数的干扰项。

questions.stem: Choose the word for blank 30.
questions.analysis:
【答案】A（官方答案）
应填 A) aesthetic
【原文】下文 Having a "beautiful" campus means green and perfectly maintained lawns along with flower beds and paved sidewalks 立刻解释了所谓 'goals' 就是把校园弄得**美观漂亮**——这正是 aesthetic（审美/美观）目标。命题人用引号 "beautiful" 直接回扣 aesthetic。
C) contaminated 被污染的目标语义颠倒：contaminated goals（被污染的目标）语义不通；高校追求的不可能是'被污染'目标，方向反了。
K) juvenile 幼稚目标与高校追求不符：juvenile goals 含贬义，高校公开追求'幼稚目标'语义荒诞，与下文美观校园语境无关。

questions.stem: Choose the word for blank 31.
questions.analysis:
【答案】D（官方答案）
应填 D) conventionally
【原文】上文 Most institutions of higher education rely on synthetic pesticides and fertilizers 说大多数高校沿用合成农药——这正是**传统/常规**管理方式；these __(31)__ managed campuses 中的 these 回指前句，因此填 conventionally（按传统方式）正好呼应。
H) incidentally 顺便地与代价主句无关：incidentally 意为'顺便提一句、偶然地'，常作插入语，无法刻画'校园被怎样管理'的方式；与下文 'come at a cost' 的因果论证脱节。

questions.stem: Choose the word for blank 32.
questions.analysis:
【答案】C（官方答案）
应填 C) contaminated
【原文】increased cancer risk, __(32)__ waterways, poisoned wildlife and lifeless soil 是命题人列出的四宗罪：增加癌症风险、__水道、毒害野生动物、贫瘠土壤。waterways 与化学品代价最自然的搭配就是 contaminated（被污染的），与 poisoned/lifeless 一同构成负面后果链。
K) juvenile 幼稚的水道语义不通：juvenile waterways（幼稚的水道）搭配不成立，且不属于负面后果范畴。

questions.stem: Choose the word for blank 33.
questions.analysis:
【答案】E（官方答案）
应填 E) emissions
【原文】as they can include petroleum-based ingredients 明示这些化学品含石油基成分，正是温室气体排放（emissions）的来源；上文 Pesticide use on college campuses also contributes to our global climate crisis 也铺垫了气候话题，indirect emissions 即'间接排放'是气候议题的标准术语。
I) infringement 侵权与石油成分无逻辑链：infringement 指权利侵犯，无法解释为何'含石油成分'会导致它增加，与气候危机话题完全无关。
L) outlet 发泄渠道与排放概念错位：outlet 虽有'出口'义，但常指情感/能量的发泄渠道或电源插座，不用于描述温室气体的间接产生，与 petroleum-based ingredients 接不上。
N) vibrations 振动与石油成分无关：vibrations 指物理振动，与气候危机、石油成分无任何因果链。

questions.stem: Choose the word for blank 34.
questions.analysis:
【答案】G（官方答案）
应填 G) hampering
【原文】decreases the life in soil, __(34)__ the ability of soils to absorb carbon or retain water，主句说减少土壤生命，分词层进一步说**妨碍**土壤吸收碳/保水的能力；hampering（妨碍）与 reducing（减少）在 and 前后形成同义递进，语义、形态都对齐。
M) rotating 旋转土壤能力语义不通：rotating the ability of soils（旋转土壤能力）搭配不成立；rotating 通常用于轮作（rotating crops）等，与本句负面后果链脱节。

questions.analysis:
【答案】O（官方答案）
应填 O) weeding
【原文】上文 Instead of using toxic chemicals 明示是有毒化学品的**替代方案**——既然不喷除草剂，那学生帮忙做的就是**人工除草**（weeding）。weed the campus grounds（给校园场地除草）也是该词的典型搭配。

passages.title: Section B 长篇阅读匹配

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: Librarians know the value of their community services, and their patrons appreciate their importance as well. But in an increasingly digital world, we see the role of libraries as community and cultural centers at times undervalued. When shrinking municipal budgets combine with the nonstop technological revolution, public library services that focus on building communities face-to-face, inspiring and educating patrons about art, literature, and music, and helping patrons engage in civil discourse can seem old-fashioned. But it is precisely those shrinking budgets and the assault of technologically mediated life that make public libraries' cultural and community offerings more important than ever.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: Many people point out the value public libraries bring to their communities. More than just books and banks of computers, libraries are still places where individuals gather to explore, interact, and imagine. Some of the specific ways in which libraries add value to our communities and serve as cultural centers for our patrons are community builders, centers for the arts, and champions of youth. Libraries serve in these capacities and are more than just about information.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: As community builders libraries are engaged in incredible work. From tiny public libraries to huge city institutions with multiple branches, libraries across the United States are building community and supporting local culture in exciting ways. These are inspiring and hopefully will encourage librarians interested in community services and cultural outreach to make connections with each other, share ideas, and build partnerships. Supporters of libraries as community builders claim that unless you are out there changing neighborhoods, you are not completing the work you are to do. Strengthening neighborhoods and championing the cultural lives of communities are big responsibilities.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: Place-based economic development stresses the importance of offering attractive, functional, and community-based places, such as libraries, in town squares and depressed neighborhoods. Like a major department store in a mall, libraries attract large numbers of people, creating economic opportunities for numerous businesses and organizations in the surrounding area. Large cities, medium-sized ones, and even small towns have successfully transformed their libraries into the hubs(枢纽) of vibrant neighborhoods.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: As key municipal agencies, and focal points for community education, libraries are major players in creating livable, environmentally friendly cities and towns. The Urban Libraries Council released a report detailing the unique ways in which libraries can further sustainability at the local level. Beyond ensuring that library construction projects consider environmental impact, libraries can take a lead in supporting local foods and craftsmen, like the Peabody Institute Library's partnering with local businesses to pioneer a farmers' market in their courtyard, or the Richmond Public Library's seed lending library which "nurtures locally-adapted plant varieties, and fosters community resilience(韧性), self-reliance and a culture of sharing."

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: Archives preserve historic artifacts, oral histories, digital history projects, and scholarly writings relevant to the community, including minority groups. Communities lucky enough to have archivists have a great advantage when it comes to organizing historical records and artifacts. An organized archive is a place where people can research their ancestry and immigration history, do environmental research, and more. An archivist is an advocate for preservation who, among other things, coordinates the restoration of maps and paintings, the digitization of vital records, and the creation of oral history projects. With projects like the Massachussets Memories Road Show and the Veterans History Project, evidence of the importance of archives is everywhere.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: In the words of Robert Putnam, "People may go to the library looking mainly for information, but they find each other there." New moms connect at baby story-times; elderly people, often facing difficult life transitions, attend events and find that they make new friends; teenagers meet up in libraries' teen spaces after school; and readers discuss current events in the periodicals room. In libraries, community-building connections are happening all the time.

paragraphs.label: H
paragraphs.text: As Keith Richards said, "The public library is the great equalizer." Despite the rising costs of concert and theater tickets, public library events (including concerts, author visits, and gallery displays) are often offered free of charge, enabling people of any income level to attend. In addition, library book groups allow people to explore and discuss the literary arts, and the Great Stories Club introduces at-risk youth to literature. The best part: it's all free and open to the public.

paragraphs.label: I
paragraphs.text: In a time when education is increasingly expensive, public libraries provide information and educational opportunities free for all people, regardless of their socio-economic status. Offered by libraries across the country, American Library Association's Let's Talk about It programs are wonderful examples of scholar-facilitated learning opportunities in libraries. In addition, many libraries present classes and discussion programs, and some even provide online continuing education courses such as the Universal Class database.

paragraphs.label: J
paragraphs.text: Librarians know that patrons aren't just information consumers, they're information producers. Patrons use the library to gain knowledge in order to create their own new and independent works. Increasing numbers of libraries provide spaces and services that meet the needs of people who want to learn how to edit Wikipedia, set up blogs or podcasts, create their own magazines, and so much more. Many libraries offer art or writing workshops and groups, and some provide music practice rooms for patrons. Programs like ImaginOn in Charlotte, North Carolina, provide exciting models that take community partnership, creativity, and creation to a new level.

paragraphs.label: K
paragraphs.text: The decline of civil discourse stems in part from the fact that it is so easy for people to watch news about, buy products from, and engage—in both the virtual and real worlds—only with those of similar backgrounds and ideologies. Public libraries, through such programs as The Human Library and Socrates Café, can help build small communities of difference that encourage people to interact with and learn from each other through dialogue. By both actively promoting civil discourse through these programs, and modeling and upholding the principles of free inquiry and expression for all, libraries help individuals rediscover the importance of and increased need for civil discourse in American life.

paragraphs.label: L
paragraphs.text: Free tutoring, homework help programs, and summer reading programs for kids and teens help bridge the economic divide that impacts students' academic performance. The cost of hiring a private tutor is well beyond what many library patrons can afford, so libraries offer homework help and tutoring online, by phone, in person, and even through social media and homework apps. Annual summer reading programs also have a positive impact on student performance and, according to a 2010 study conducted by Dominican University's Graduate School of Library and Information Science, students' reading skills get a boost from these popular nationwide events.

paragraphs.label: M
paragraphs.text: Through library collections, programs, and physical spaces, children learn to share, to be engaged in their communities, to participate in the arts, and to explore their immediate world and the world at large. There are surely endless examples of innovative library services for children, including the Middle Country Public Library's Nature Explorium, which engages children in learning about the natural world.

paragraphs.label: N
paragraphs.text: These examples are just a few of the many amazing things that public libraries around the United States (and the world) are doing to build and maintain strong community connections. We encourage you to try some of these ideas in your own libraries, and we hope that these ideas will help you be better able to convince your community leaders of the important role that public libraries play in communities large and small.

2025年6月英语六级真题第1套 长篇阅读（信息匹配） 第 1 篇 38. With the costs of education continually rising, public libraries remain places where all people can have access to education. 这句陈述的信息出自第几段？为什么？ 2025年6月英语六级真题第1套 长篇阅读（信息匹配） 第 1 篇 第 38 句的信息出自 I 段（强锚点句）。I 段定位句为「In a time when education is increasingly expensive, public libraries provide information and educational opportunities free for all people, regardless of their socio-economic status.」（在教育越来越昂贵的时代，公共图书馆免费向所有人提供信息与教育机会，无论其社会经济地位如何。）。陈述句是对原文的同义改写（With the costs of education continually rising ↔ In a time when education is increasingly expensive；public libraries remain places where all people can have access to education ↔ public libraries provide information and educational opportunities free for all people, regardless of their socio-economic status）。与之话题相邻的 H 段、L 段虽含相近关键词，但并非该信息的真正出处，需逐一排除。

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: Nationally, one in six children miss 15 or more days of school in a year. Education officials have deplored all this missed instruction.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: These chronically absent students suffer academically because of all the classroom instruction they miss out on. In 2015, the U.S. secretary of education responded to this crisis, urging communities to support every student to attend every day and be successful in school. His open letter stated that missing 10% of school days in a year for any reason—excused or unexcused—is a primary cause of low academic achievement.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: Worrying about whether children attend school makes sense. After all, if students don't show up, teachers can't teach them.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: But what if America's attendance crisis is about much more than students missing class? What if, instead, it is a reflection of family and community crises these students face—such as being ejected from the family apartment, fearing for their safety in their neighborhood or suffering an illness?

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: As social scientists we investigated how excused and unexcused absences relate to children's academic achievement.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: We find that absences excused by a parent do little to harm children's learning. In fact, children with no unexcused absences—but 15 to 18 excused absences—have test scores equal to their peers who have no absences.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: Meanwhile, the average child with even just one unexcused absence does much worse academically than peers with none.

paragraphs.label: H
paragraphs.text: We believe unexcused absence is a strong signal of the many challenges children and families face, including economic and medical hardships. Unexcused absences can be a powerful signal of how those out-of-school challenges affect children's academic progress.

paragraphs.label: I
paragraphs.text: Our evidence suggests unexcused absences are problematic, but for a different reason than people often think. Absence from school, and especially unexcused absence, matters mainly as a signal of many crises children and their families may be facing. It matters less as a cause of lower student achievement due to missed instruction.

paragraphs.label: J
paragraphs.text: How we choose to think of school absences matters for educational policy. School attendance policies typically hold schools and families accountable for the days children miss, regardless of whether they were excused or unexcused absences.

paragraphs.label: K
paragraphs.text: These policies assume that missing school for any reason harms children academically because they are missing classroom instruction. They also assume that schools will be able to effectively intervene by reducing student absences. We find neither to be the case.

paragraphs.label: L
paragraphs.text: As a result, these attendance policies end up disproportionately punishing families dealing with out-of-school crises in their lives and pressuring schools who serve them to get students to school more often.

paragraphs.label: M
paragraphs.text: We instead suggest using unexcused absence from school as a signal to channel resources to the children and families who need them most.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: After earning a bachelor's degree, I was determined to do what I love. I headed straight to graduate school to investigate the social problems that fascinated me.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: For almost a decade, I told everyone I encountered that they should do the same. "Follow your passion," I counseled. "You can figure out the employment stuff later."

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: It wasn't until I began to research this widely accepted career advice that I understood how problematic it really was.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: As a sociologist, I interviewed college students and professional workers to learn what it really meant to pursue their dreams, which I will refer to here as the passion principle. I was stunned by what I found out about this principle in the research for my new book.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: Surveys show the American public has long held the passion principle in high regard as a career decision-making priority. And its popularity is even stronger among those facing job instability.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: Advocates of the passion principle found it compelling because they believed that following one's passion can provide workers with both the motivation necessary to work hard and a place to find fulfillment.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: Yet, what I found is that following one's passion does not necessarily lead to fulfillment, but is one of the most powerful cultural forces perpetuating overwork. I also found that promoting the pursuit of one's passion helps perpetuate social inequalities due to the fact that not everyone has the same economic resources to allow them to pursue their passion with ease.

paragraphs.label: H
paragraphs.text: While the passion principle is broadly popular, not everyone has the necessary resources to turn their passion into a stable, good-paying job. Passion-seekers from wealthy families are better able to wait until a job they are passionate about comes along without worrying about student loans in the meantime. They are also better situated to take unpaid internships to get their foot in the door while their parents pay their rent. And they often have access to parents' social networks to help them find jobs. Surveys revealed that working-class and first-generation college graduates, regardless of their career field, are more likely than their wealthier peers to end up in low-paying unskilled jobs when they pursue their passion.

paragraphs.label: I
paragraphs.text: Colleges, workplaces and career counselors who promote the "follow your passion" path for everyone, without leveling the playing field, help perpetuate socioeconomic inequalities among career aspirants.

paragraphs.label: J
paragraphs.text: It's not just well-off passion-seekers who benefit from the passion principle. Employers of passionate workers do, too. Potential employers showed greater interest in passionate applicants in part because they believed the applicants would work hard at their jobs without expecting an increase in pay. They even sacrifice a good salary, job stability and leisure time to work in a job they love.

The Tiangong Space Station, China's first space laboratory, boasts over 110 cubic meters of usable space and is able to accommodate three astronauts, orbiting at an altitude of 400 to 450 kilometers above the Earth's surface. The station has carried out more than 180 scientific research and application projects, covering such fields as space life science, space medicine, and space materials science. The research achievements of the station have been widely applied in China and have generated remarkable economic benefits. For example, the direct economic benefits created by space breeding reach hundreds of billions of yuan. This not only marks China's tremendous progress in aerospace technology, but also demonstrates that China has made significant contributions to global space research and application.
